patterns.condition: Designing an adventure or RPG map
patterns.action: Cycle: explore, meet a challenge (fight, talk, solve), earn a reward, grow, face harder content. Every system should feed growth or choice.
patterns.statement: Growth and choice drive the loop

patterns.action: Give each quest a state (available, active, complete, turned in), advance it only from game events, and keep the progress for each player.
patterns.statement: A quest is a small state machine

patterns.action: Save progress, currency and unlocks in persistable data for each player with a version number, so an update never wipes them.

patterns.condition: Stats that come from levels and gear
patterns.action: Keep base stats and gear separate and compute the final value when needed, so removing an item can never leave a stale bonus.
patterns.statement: Final numbers should be computed, not stored

patterns.action: Use a simple rule where each level needs a bit more than the last, set the target hours per level, and check the top level against your health and damage scales.
patterns.statement: Experience curves must flatten, not explode

patterns.action: Hold lines in a list with choices and conditions, run them with one small routine, and keep display text out of the logic so it can be edited.
Make each choice change something later (a flag, a reward, an ending), or keep only the choices that matter.
Tell the player what to do next with a quest marker or a screen line at every step.

patterns.condition: An escape room or puzzle map
patterns.action: Map the solution as a chain where each puzzle unlocks the next and its hint can be found in the room first, then test it with someone who has not seen it.
patterns.statement: Puzzles need a clear chain of clues

patterns.condition: A puzzle uses consumable items or one way doors
patterns.action: Make every required item obtainable again or not consumable, and give a reset or hint path so no state is unwinnable.
Store solved flags in one manager and drive doors from it, so a player who joins late sees the same progress.
patterns.statement: Puzzle state belongs to the team

patterns.action: Play from a clean state through every quest, reload midway, and confirm the progress persisted.
patterns.statement: Test the quest line from a fresh player
